messages:
alex: FYI customer alpha-inc hit a sudden promo spike and started getting 429s + latency spikes. They report header x-burst-credits: 0 and x-burst-reset ~22s. Any quick mitigations?

maria: Can you paste the exact headers + a short description of the request pattern? Burst credits vs hard quota matters.

alex: Pasted from the response: x-burst-credits: 0, x-burst-limit: 1000, x-burst-reset: 22, x-rate-limit-remaining: 0. Pattern: ~600 small chat requests (50-200 tokens) over 30s from a single API key.

kevin: This looks like burst credit exhaustion (not the monthly quota). Short-term options: 1) smooth on client side (throttle/leaky-bucket), 2) fallback to a smaller model variant that uses separate capacity, 3) enable server-side smoothing for this tenant, or 4) one-time emergency burst top-up from billing.

sara: We can do an emergency top-up but need account owner sign-off. @billing please confirm process and ETA. :hourglass: 

billing: We can approve a one-time grant for production accounts. Need account owner email + explicit ok in the ticket. ETA ~15-30m once we have confirmation.

kevin: For immediate mitigation, recommend implementing client-side smoothing + backoff. Example quick curl retry (exponential backoff + small jitter):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
URL="https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
KEY="$API_KEY"
for i in {1..10}; do
  resp=$(curl -s -o /dev/stderr -w '%{http_code}' -X POST $URL -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":50}')
  if [ "$resp" -eq 429 ]; then
    sleep_time=$((2**$i + RANDOM%3))
    echo "429, backing off $sleep_time s"
    sleep $sleep_time
  else
    break
  fi
done
```

maria: I'll send these repro steps to the customer and recommend they add a client-side leaky-bucket that spaces requests to the API. Also suggest using streaming to reduce NPS per-request cost.

alex: Repro script (node) I used locally to reproduce:

```js
// simple spike generator
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const KEY = process.env.API_KEY;
for (let i=0;i<600;i++) {
  fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: 'x'.repeat(20), max_tokens: 40 })
  }).then(r => r.text()).then(t => console.log(i, t.slice(0,80))).catch(e => console.error('err', e));
}
```

kevin: For server-side tuning we can flip a tenant-level smoothing flag. Quick config we use in infra for smoothing: 

```yaml
burst_smoothing: enabled
window_seconds: 60
refill_per_second: 8  # how many burst credits refill each sec
max_burst_multiplier: 3  # headroom factor before 429s
policy: drop_or_queue  # options: drop, queue, degrade_to_smaller_model
```

kevin: If we enable degrade_to_smaller_model, traffic above smoothing thresholds is routed to a lower-cost model that has its own burst pool. That reduces 429 surface without blocking.

ops-bot: Incident created: TICKET-4521 (support) -> assigned to maria, kevin.

maria: Opening the billing ticket now and emailing the account owner for sign-off. Also adding recommended client-side patch to the support reply.

alex: Thanks — I'll keep the customer in the loop. Will update here when billing confirms or when I see traffic back to normal. :thumbsup:
